### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **41** documentable anchor(s).

**38** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **57** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5e52e5b2188f1a5703de3abbc2ad08e14bcd65b4` — the merge of head `1d394b81c310005c5f54f36fe9113623fb8fcdf0` into base `404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5e52e5b2188f1a5703de3abbc2ad08e14bcd65b4 && git checkout 5e52e5b2188f1a5703de3abbc2ad08e14bcd65b4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc 1d394b81c310005c5f54f36fe9113623fb8fcdf0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc && git merge --no-ff 1d394b81c310005c5f54f36fe9113623fb8fcdf0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 404fc477e52f30aa9b77cd2ad52f7adb0e3009fc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1d394b81c310005c5f54f36fe9113623fb8fcdf0`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23224 (body and all 8 comments, 6144021196 through 6152923496), #23266's body and its 3 comments (ruling 6148183570 read in full), PR #23321 (body, the 15-file list, the three-dot diff against `main`, with file content read at the head through `git show`), and the head's check-runs read at 2026-10-13T19:11Z: 32 completed (26 success; 6 skipped: the docs build, the console pin gate, the dogfood shards and CLI, temporal conformance, the opt-in tarball smoke) and 7 in progress (Test Core 1/6 to 6/6, Type Check · workspace). The in-progress runs are not judged here and this record does not vouch for them; landing precondition ② (every check green) is the seat's own re-read before arming. Judged against `contract-review.md`, the Clause-② lines of `execution-duties.md`, ADR-0138 D1/D3/D4 and its E1 row, ADR-0090 D9/D11, and ruling C.

### ① Derived judgments

**Published surface.** `@objectstack/core`'s root entry (`.` maps to `dist/index.d.ts`, whose source does `export * from './security/index.js'`) gains ten additive bindings, each named by the changeset:
- `resolveGuestOrganization` — D4's organization step, one step with two askers (the guest entry and the CRUD gate). Right.
- `resolveSystemWriteOrganization`, `SystemWriteOrganizationDecision`, `SystemWriteRefusalReason` — the ADR-0131 D9 predicate relocated one layer down with its decision table unchanged (a wall refuses; zero refuses `no-organization` or, with no organization object registered, `no-organization-object`; one derives; several refuse `ambiguous-organization`). Right: D4 item 2 forbids a second spelling and `core` cannot import `objectql`.
- `GuestOrganizationUnresolvedError`, `isGuestOrganizationUnresolvedError`, `GUEST_ORGANIZATION_UNRESOLVED_CODE`, `GUEST_ORGANIZATION_UNRESOLVED_STATUS`, `GUEST_ORGANIZATION_UNRESOLVED_MESSAGE`, `GuestOrganizationRefusalReason` — right. The code `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` is a member of the ADR-0112 catalog (`packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts` in `StandardErrorCode`; `error-code-ledger.zod.ts` at 501), so no new code enters the ledger and the "new code is always yes" rule is not what makes this `yes`. The recogniser compares `code` and `name`, never `instanceof`, which holds across a package boundary. Right.
- `ResolveAuthzInput.guestEntry?: boolean` — an optional field on an exported input type, additive and named ("the new `guestEntry` input"). Right.
- No name collision: Type Check · source gates is green on the head, where an `export *` ambiguity would have failed.

`@objectstack/objectql`: `tenancy/system-write-organization.ts` re-exports the three bindings from core; the barrel's `resolveSystemWriteOrganization` and its two types keep their names and resolve to core's one function (identity pinned in `system-write-organization.test.ts`). Nothing a consumer imports moves. Right. `plugin-security`, `plugin-sharing`, `runtime`: no export moves (`isGuestPrincipal` is module-private; `refuseGuestWithoutOrganization` and `guestOrganizationRefusalWarned` are private members). Right.

**Accept set.** No `packages/spec` path; no authorable key, stored shape or response field moves; the ADR-0087 disposition `none` matches the E1 row verbatim. Right. The behaviour changes are runtime security-boundary changes (Clause ②'s negative boundary), each judged against the record:
- D3 item 1 — the guest's sets are read by `positionBoundSetNames`, factored out of `resolveUserAuthzGrants` and now the one reader both paths call. Right.
- D3 item 2 — nothing bound: no set, no organization, no read issued (core pin asserts the engine saw zero reads). Right.
- D3 item 3 — `resolvePermissionSetsForContextUnmemoized` drops the guest's `positions` from the request (`isGuest` = `principalKind: 'guest'` with no `userId`), closing the name fold for the guest; the baseline attaches only to a caller with a `userId`; `everyone` lives in the user path a guest never reaches. `permissionSetMemoKey` carries `principalKind` and the presence of `userId`, so a guest and a human holding `positions: ['guest']` never share a memo entry. Right, with human controls in the unit file.
- D3 item 7 and D4 — the order in `resolveGuestAnchorGrants` is definition (in-process), then organization, then ledger, then bodies; nothing is granted without a `derived` decision, and the only row read before the decision is the organization probe itself. Right.
- D4 item 1 — `ctx.tenantId` for a guest is written only from `guest.organizationId`; the `tenantId` the session and API-key paths derive is assigned after the anonymous branch has already returned, so nothing the client sends names the guest's organization, and `tenancyPosture` is deployment configuration. Right.
- D4 item 3 — the refusal is raised at the CRUD gate (`resolveOperationPrincipals`, after the principal-less check and ahead of the fail-closed catch that would mask it as 403), not at the entry, so every 401 domain and the flow door (class 5) stay untouched. Right. Dropping the rule's own `isSystem` read in commit 5283490390 is sound: both callers return for a system context first.
- D4 "refused, loudly, naming the missing site binding" — the message names the site binding and both remedies and discloses no organization count or posture (the unit pin asserts the message carries no id, reason or count). 501 over 403 keeps an ungranted guest and an unresolvable deployment distinguishable, which is what a located refusal is for. Right.
- Ruling C (6148183570) — `SharingService.buildReadFilter` answers `{ id: '__deny_all__' }` for the guest principal after `shouldBypass` (the system bypass and the platform bypass list) and before the sharing-model branch and its owner-less and phantom-anchor fall-throughs, so `private`, `public_read`, `public_read_write` and `controlled_by_parent` each read 0 rows (5 unit shapes with member and system controls; 6 door pins with admin controls). `resolveSharingReadFilter` spreads the context into the call, so the analytics path meets the same guard. Share links are redeemed at their own door and never pass this filter (door control: the linked record is read; eligibility held at the mint, 422, and at redemption, 404). No `externalSharingModel` reader was added (#23268 stays its own card). Right.
- The write gates (`buildWriteFilter`, `checkEdit`, `checkDelete`) keep the OWD branch for a guest. Judged acceptable, not a gap: the anchor tier (`describeAnchorForbiddenBits` over `describeHighPrivilegeBits`, read at the head) refuses `allowEdit`, `allowDelete`, `allowTransfer`, `allowExport`, view-all and modify-all, and any `systemPermissions` for `guest`, so a tier-conformant binding never reaches those gates; create is the one case-by-case write and it takes no row filter. The residual is in ③.
- `runtime`: `resolveExecutionContext` is the one face passing `guestEntry: true`; the other faces that call `resolveAuthzContext` (rest-server, mcp, sharing-plugin, settings, storage, datasource admin routes, marketplace install) omit it and stay fail-closed, matching D2's "everything else answers 401". Right.
- The reference-app count: 0 bindings start granting and 0 fold grants stop, pinned by the dogfood census over app-showcase, app-crm and app-multi-package with a fixture control; app-todo declares neither positions nor sets. The changeset names them, per the row. Right.
- `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gains one row for the new unit file's pinned `findOne`, written by the gate's own `--write`: a record the gate requires, not a widened exemption. Right.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23224-guest-grants-channel.md`: `@objectstack/core: minor`; `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/runtime`: `patch`. This matches what the diff publishes: only core's exported index widens (ten additive bindings; nothing removed or narrowed), and the other four move no export and change behaviour only under the accepted record and ruling C. `skip-changeset` does not apply. The changeset's row-scope sentences state ruling C ("returns no row, whatever the object's sharing model"; "the guest reaches a record only through a share link"), its ADR-0087 line reads `none`, and it names the bindings that start granting, as the E1 row requires. Check Changeset is green on the head.

`Clause-②:` — the PR body's second line reads `Clause-②: yes`, and the governing claim 6146352069 reads `Clause-②: yes` (the first claim's `no` was corrected by the hand-off's measured fork 5 and the re-claim). Right: the published surface widens, so a contract-tier review is owed before the queue, and this record is that review. No governed surface is in the file list (Governed Surface Queue Guard green), so this record is the Clause-② control and not a Tier S one.

### ③ Boundary flags

Hand-off 6145588579, `open_questions`:
1. Row scope (D3 item 6 against ADR-0090 D9/D11) — ruled C on #23266 (6148183570, 「同意」); applied here at `buildReadFilter`, pinned at unit and door with the link control. Answered.
2. No authoring door for a `guest` binding — filed as #23267, re-pointed to this card by triage 6148511128, held undispatched until E1 lands (ruling item 4). Escalated, outside this PR.
3. The refusal code — `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, a catalog member as D4 requires; judged right in ①. Answered.
4. A walled deployment with exactly one organization — D9's refusal kept, per D4 item 2 (one predicate, no second spelling). It fails closed, and a deployment that needs the derivation is F2/D5's demand. Answered, no escalation.
5. The `Clause-②` line — flipped to `yes` at the re-claim. Answered.

Final report 6152923496, `open_questions: []`; its deviations, each judged:
- `sharing-service.ts` and its test outside the claim's files — ruling C's one site, pre-declared by PM direction 6149308636 ("the file surface grows by that one site"), and the dev named it. Answered.
- The ledger row, the 4 comment lines and the dropped `isSystem` read in `security-plugin.ts`, the unit double's refusal of an unimplemented combinator, and the dogfood slot typing — gate-driven, each judged right in ①.
- A2d (measured at df4be9b562) and A5 (at 02caf8afc6) not re-run on the final head — verified by reading: `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/` has no commit after 02caf8afc6, and the fold hunk of `security-plugin.ts` is identical between df4be9b562 and the head (only the refusal's `isSystem` line and the S8 merge moved there, and the unit legs A1 to A4 were re-run at the head). The measurements carry.
- Two merges of `main`, five commits behind at the final derivation — the queue rebuilds on the current `main`; no overlap claimed, none seen in the file list.
- `check:query-options-erasure` re-run alone after a battery timeout — the head's own scoped run is green.
- Commit trailers and background commands — outside the contract.

Out-of-scope findings and acceptance notes:
- The platform bypass list (`sys_user`, `sys_organization`, `sys_member`, `sys_record_share`, `sys_user_permission_set`) skips record scoping for the guest too. A real reach question, not E1's: ruling C closes the OWD branch, not the platform bypass, and whether a `guest` set may name those objects is the anchor tier's (`describeAnchorForbiddenBits` does not refuse them today). Escalated to #23267 by the dev's carrier line; the seat owes that card the pointer when it dispatches it.
- The write gates take the OWD branch for a guest — unreachable under the tier, verified at the head. Residual: if the tier ever admits an edit bit case by case, `buildWriteFilter`, `checkEdit` and `checkDelete` need the same guard. Noted; no card today (zero pull, no door).
- The form doors on a multi-organization deployment keep their own `500 ERR_SYSTEM_WRITE_ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED` — D4 item 4 keeps them; pinned unchanged. Right.
- Record text: ADR-0138 D3 item 6 still reads "through the object's declared sharing model" until the Tier H one-sentence amendment lands (#23266's remainder, transition 6149341777). The code cites the ruling by comment id at both sites and the changeset states the ruled scope, so the reversal is on record, not quiet (Prime Directive 13); the ruling binds no order between this PR and the amendment. The seat owes the amendment PR promptly.
